title: Completed normalization branches and component ideals at a split node
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a reduced local $k$-algebra (no nonzero nilpotents), essentially of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra], of Krull dimension $1$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], with a fixed isomorphism $\widehat A\cong R:=k[[u,v]]/(uv)$ of complete local $k$-algebras. Completions are maximal-ideal-adic [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] and formal power series are [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. For any reduced ring $E$, write $Q(E)$ for its localization at all non-zero-divisors, where $s$ is a non-zero-divisor when $se=0$ implies $e=0$, and let $\widetilde E$ be its integral closure in $Q(E)$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure].
The map $R\to N:=k[[u]]\times k[[v]]$ is $h\mapsto(h(u,0),h(0,v))$. Its image is the pairs having equal constant term, $N=R+R(1,0)$ is finite integral over $R$, $Q(R)=k((u))\times k((v))$, and $\widetilde R=N$. Here $k((u))$ and $k((v))$ are the fraction fields of the indicated one-variable power-series domains.
Put $D=\widetilde A$. Then $D$ is finite over $A$, and $D\otimes_A\widehat A\cong N$ compatibly with $A\to\widehat A$. There are exactly two maximal ideals $\mathfrak n_u,\mathfrak n_v$ of $D$ over $\mathfrak m$, both with residue field $k$, and the completed maps $\widehat A\to\widehat{D_{\mathfrak n_u}},\widehat{D_{\mathfrak n_v}}$ are, respectively, $u\mapsto t,v\mapsto0$ and $u\mapsto0,v\mapsto t$ into $k[[t]]$.
For each minimal prime $P$ of $A$ (a prime minimal among prime ideals), put $D_P=\widetilde{A/P}$. There are compatible identifications $Q(A)=\prod_P\operatorname{Frac}(A/P)$ and $D=\prod_PD_P$; on scheme affine charts these identifications commute with localization [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Under $\widehat A=R$, the completed quotient is $\widehat{A/P}=R/P\widehat A$, and exactly one of the following occurs: $A$ is a domain, $P=0$ is its only minimal prime and $P\widehat A=0$; or $A$ has exactly two minimal primes whose extended ideals are $(u)$ and $(v)$. In the first case both normalization points belong to that component; in the second case each belongs to a different component, with exactly one point on each $\operatorname{Spec}D_P$ over $\mathfrak m/P$. Thus the completions of the reduced components are respectively $R$, or the two rings $k[[u]]$ and $k[[v]]$.

proof.text: Write $A=W^{-1}B$ with $B$ a finite-type $k$-algebra, as permitted by the hypothesis. A field is Noetherian since its only ideals are zero and the whole field. The finite-type and localization Noetherian permanence statements therefore make $A$ Noetherian. All subsequent Noetherian local completion results apply to $(A,\mathfrak m)$.

Apply the formal-node axes calculation to the fixed presentation of $R$. It gives the injective axis map, identifies $R$ with its equal-constant-term image $S\subset N$, and identifies $Q(R)$ with $k((u))\times k((v))$ compatibly with the inclusions of $R$ and $N$. The equal-constant normalization theorem, applied to this $S$ inside $L=k((u))\times k((v))$, says that $N=S+S\epsilon$ with $\epsilon=(1,0)$, so $N=R+R(1,0)$ is finite over $R$, and that the integral closure of $S$ in $L$ is exactly $N$; in particular $N$ is integral over $R$. Transporting through the two compatible identifications gives $\widetilde R=N$ inside the specified total fraction ring, with the specified structural map.

The normalization-completion theorem applies directly to the reduced, essentially finite-type, one-dimensional local $k$-algebra $A$. It makes $D$ finite over $A$ and canonically identifies $C:=D\otimes_A R$ with $\widetilde R=N$, compatibly with $A\to R$ and the inclusions into total fraction rings. The finite-algebra Noetherian theorem makes $D$ Noetherian. Every maximal ideal of $D$ lies over $\mathfrak m$ by the finite-algebra local-radical statement. Conversely a prime $\mathfrak q$ of $D$ over $\mathfrak m$ is maximal: $D/\mathfrak q$ is a domain that is a finite-dimensional vector space over the field $A/\mathfrak m$, and multiplication by a nonzero element is an injective, hence surjective, linear endomorphism. So the primes of $D$ over $\mathfrak m$ are exactly its maximal ideals. The finite-extension completion theorem, applied with base prime $\mathfrak m$, now gives
$$N=C=\prod_{\mathfrak n\mid\mathfrak m}\widehat{D_{\mathfrak n}}$$
as $R$-algebras. The factors are nonzero local rings, and their residue fields are those of $D_{\mathfrak n}$, by the local-completion local-ring theorem, since localizations of the Noetherian ring $D$ are Noetherian.

A local ring has only the idempotents $0,1$: if $a^2=a$, one of $a,1-a$ is a unit and forces the other to be zero. Consequently a finite product of nonzero local rings has one primitive idempotent for each factor. The displayed $N=k[[u]]\times k[[v]]$ has precisely two such idempotents $(1,0),(0,1)$, so the preceding product has exactly two factors. Label the corresponding ideals $\mathfrak n_u,\mathfrak n_v$ so that projection to their completed local rings is projection to the $u$- and $v$-factor of $N$. The factor isomorphisms are $R$-linear, hence the completed maps send $(u,v)$ to $(t,0)$ and $(0,t)$ respectively. Their residue fields are $k$, so the preceding residue-field comparison gives $D/\mathfrak n_u=D/\mathfrak n_v=k$.

proof.text: The reduced-Noetherian total-fractions theorem identifies $Q(A)$ with the finite product of $A_P$ over the minimal primes $P$. Its assertion that $PA_P=0$ identifies $A_P$ with $\operatorname{Frac}(A/P)$: every nonzero element of $A/P$ is represented by an element outside $P$, which is inverted in $A_P$. Integrality of a tuple over $A$ is equivalent to integrality of its coordinates over $A/P$. Indeed, a monic polynomial over $A$ projects to each quotient; conversely choose a monic annihilating polynomial for each coordinate over $A/P$, lift its coefficients to $A$, and multiply the finitely many lifted polynomials. In each coordinate one factor vanishes. Thus $D=\prod_P D_P$. Each $D_P$ is finite over $A$, being a direct summand of the finite module $D$, and embeds $A/P$ into its fraction field. The identifications respect localization: on fractions all maps send $a/s$ to the coordinate fractions. Integral closure commutes with localization by the cited localization theorem. Localizing a finite product retains precisely those field factors whose minimal prime misses the multiplicative set; the other factors become zero. Applying the same total-fractions theorem to the reduced Noetherian localized ring identifies these retained factors with its total fractions. This proves the requested compatibility on affine charts.

For each $P$ put $C_P=D_P\otimes_A R$. These are the factors of $D\otimes_A R=N$. Each $C_P$ is nonzero: the nonzero finite $A$-algebra $D_P$ has a maximal ideal, all such ideals lie over $\mathfrak m$, and the finite-extension completion theorem expresses $C_P$ as a nonempty product of completed local rings. These completions are nonzero by the local-completion residue-field assertion (use Noetherian permanence for $D_P$ and its localizations). Let $e_P\in D$ be the idempotent selecting $D_P$. Its image in $N$ is therefore nonzero. These images are orthogonal and sum to $1$. Since idempotents in each power-series domain are only $0,1$, they partition the two coordinates of $N$ into nonempty subsets. Thus there are either one or two minimal primes. In the one-prime case $A\hookrightarrow Q(A)=\operatorname{Frac}(A/P)$ has kernel $P$, so $P=0$ and $A$ is a domain. In the two-prime case the two $C_P$ are exactly the separate factors of $N$.

source.place: Tag 0E38 (lemma-closed-subscheme-nodal-curve), component-versus-branch argument; algebra.tex Tag 07N9 and the local completion residue-field statements.

proof.text: It remains to identify the extended component ideals, rather than just count them. The completion map $A\to R$ is flat by the local faithfully-flat completion theorem. By the definition of flatness, tensoring the injection $A/P\hookrightarrow D_P$ with $R$ is injective. Since $(A/P)\otimes_A R=R/PR$ (send $\bar a\otimes r$ to $ar$ modulo $PR$), the kernel of $R\to C_P$ is exactly $PR$. If there are two minimal primes, the preceding coordinate partition identifies these kernels as $(v)$ for the $u$-factor and $(u)$ for the $v$-factor. If there is one prime it is zero, so its extended ideal is zero. The local-completion quotient theorem applied to $A\twoheadrightarrow A/P$ identifies $\widehat{A/P}=R/PR$ with its actual completed quotient map. These are consequently $R$ in the domain case, and $k[[u]],k[[v]]$ in the two-component case.

source.place: Tag 0E38 (lemma-closed-subscheme-nodal-curve), completed quotient maps; algebra.tex Tags 00MC (lemma-completion-faithfully-flat), 00HB (definition-flat), 00MA (lemma-completion-tensor).

proof.text: Finally the factor $D_P=e_PD$ corresponds on spectra to the component selected by $e_P$. The completed normalization point indexed by a coordinate belongs to this factor exactly when the image of $e_P$ in that coordinate is $1$: modulo the corresponding maximal ideal this idempotent has the same value, since the completion map preserves residue fields. With one $P$ its image is $(1,1)$, so both points belong to that component. With two $P$ the images are $(1,0)$ and $(0,1)$, so each component has exactly one of the two normalization points. A maximal ideal of any $D_P$ over $\mathfrak m/P$ gives, by projection $D\to D_P$, a maximal ideal of $D$ over $\mathfrak m$, and conversely. The preceding exhaustive list of two points therefore proves also the asserted uniqueness on each component.
